narrative:
The model estimates a 76% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your total years of professional experience, the length of time you have spent in your current organization, and whether you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your 11+ years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While only 14.7% of employees predicted to stay have this much experience, the model sees longer careers as a signal that people are more likely to move on. Similarly, having spent 1-5 years in your current role (a common tenure among stayers) also contributed toward predicting departure, as the combination of solid overall experience with relatively short organizational tenure often indicates someone ready for a change. Finally, the fact that you have received other job opportunities during your time here was another notable push toward leaving, since external offers frequently precede actual exits.

Given these insights, the organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You might consider what would increase your sense of stability and recognition here, while the company could explore ways to better retain experienced talent like yourself before external opportunities become too attractive.
